labels.label: lem:gluing-estimate

hypotheses.paper: (Σ̄, ḡ) smooth closed; Σ ⊂ Σ̄ a compact domain with ∂Σ = ⊔ B_j; D_j the closures of the components of Σ̄ ∖ Σ, each meeting Σ along B_j (l.650)
hypotheses.note: Σ is the MeasuredModel M of Yamabe.Quotient with a CurvedMetric g (Yamabe.Kobayashi). The D_j form a Filling: one MeasuredModel Y E N 1 each (one boundary component) and a measurable map glue j : X → Y identifying B_j ⊂ ∂Σ with ∂D_j. Σ̄ itself is not modelled; it is read through its pieces. 'Meeting along B_j' is BoundaryMatch: glue j pushes bvol_h on B_j to bvol_h̄ on ∂D_j (carried).
IsFiniteMeasure of vol_g, vol_h and every bvol_h j.
not used.
vol_g ≠ 0 and bvol_g j ≠ 0, which give Vol(Σ, h) > 0 and A_j > 0 (vol_conformal_pos, bvol_conformal_pos).

R_g, H_g are data of CurvedMetric (as in Yamabe.Kobayashi). DensityMeasurable asks the densities √det G and √det(Pᵀ G P) to be a.e.-measurable (FrameMetric carries no measurability, and the conformal identities need it).
MinimalBoundary (bvol_g j-a.e.).
y ≤ 0, where the real y stands for Y_[ḡ](Σ̄). It enters only through thm:yamabe (b), i.e. R_h̄ = c = y·Vol(Σ̄, h̄)^{-2/N} (IsYamabeMetric). It is used only for 'the last term is non-positive'.

gluing_estimate takes any β with β_j ≤ EHB(D_j, h̄|_{D_j}) (BoundaryYamabe, carried). gluing_estimate_YB takes β_j = the model's YB_[g_j](D_j) (eq:boundary-yamabe through the conformal law), reads '> −∞' as BddBelow of the competitors' energies, and derives BoundaryYamabe (YB_le_EHB) from the boundary conformal law on D_j (ConformalLawB, l.330, carried).
gluing_estimate: any m ≤ 0 with m ≤ R_g vol_g-a.e. The printed m (CurvedMetric.kobM) is in lem_gluing_estimate and gluing_estimate_YB.

hypotheses.paper: thm:yamabe (b): ψ > 0 smooth on Σ̄, h̄ = ψ^{4/(N−2)} ḡ, R_h̄ = Y_[ḡ](Σ̄) Vol(Σ̄, h̄)^{−2/N} (l.658)
hypotheses.note: cited. u and h̄ = (body, cap) are given. IsConformal: Pos u and body.G = u^{4/(N−2)} • g.G on Σ. IsYamabeMetric: R_h̄ = c a.e. on Σ and on every D_j, and c = y·volBar^{−2/N}. On the D_j no conformal relation is needed by the chain.

Pos u (val u > 0 everywhere); val u a.e.-strongly measurable for vol_g; tr u a.e.-strongly measurable for bvol_g j; tr u = val u bvol_g j-a.e. (the trace of a function continuous up to ∂Σ is its boundary value).

hypotheses.paper: lem:kobayashi (a) applied to EH(Σ, h), h = u^{4/(N−2)} g (l.658–661)
hypotheses.note: the identification of EH(Σ, h), computed from h's own curvatures, with the conformal quotient of u over g is the conformal law eq:conformal-energy-bdry (l.326–328, cited MR1152225, MR1173925), carried as ConformalLaw. Kobayashi (a) itself is the strict Yamabe.MeasuredModel.kobayashi.
MeanCurvatureFlip, pointwise bvol_h j-a.e. through glue j; integrated in integral_flip.

hypotheses.paper: 'by definition of the boundary Yamabe constant', EHB(D_j, h̄) ≥ β_j (l.663–666)
hypotheses.note: BoundaryYamabe in gluing_estimate; derived in gluing_estimate_YB (see β_j).

hypotheses.paper: Vol(Σ̄, h̄) = Vol(Σ, h̄) + Σ_j Vol(D_j, h̄) (l.672)
hypotheses.note: Filling.volBar is defined as this sum.
proved from body.G = u^{4/(N−2)} g.G: vol_conformal_univ, bvol_conformal_univ, normSq_pStar_conformal, normSq_pSharp_conformal.

hypotheses.paper: h̄ is a Yamabe metric of [ḡ] (l.655)
hypotheses.note: only its consequence from thm:yamabe (b) is used (constant scalar curvature c = y·Vol^{−2/N}). The statements hold for every such h̄.

questions: Σ̄ is read through its pieces. Vol(Σ̄, h̄) is the sum of the pieces' volumes (l.672 as a definition), and Y_[ḡ](Σ̄) is a real y, tied to h̄ only by thm:yamabe (b), c = y·Vol(Σ̄, h̄)^{−2/N} (l.658). The closed manifold, its conformal class and its Yamabe constant are not modelled. Is this reading of Σ̄ acceptable for the abstract layer (OQ-44), or should Σ̄ be a closed MeasuredModel of its own, with restriction maps and additivity as a hypothesis?

The statement's 'there exists a smooth positive function u on Σ such that … where h̄ is a Yamabe metric of [ḡ]' (l.650–655). Reading taken: for any Yamabe metric h̄ = ψ^{4/(N−2)} ḡ, the inequality holds with u = ψ|_Σ (lem_gluing_estimate states the ∃ with that witness). For Y_[ḡ](Σ̄) ≤ 0 the Yamabe metric is unique up to homothety (prop:csc-yamabe (a)), and the ratio Vol(Σ̄, h̄)/Vol(Σ, h̄) is scale-invariant, so the readings agree.

'β_j > −∞' is read as: the boundary conformal energies of the competitors of YB_[g_j](D_j) are bounded below (BddBelow). Lean's real sInf of a set unbounded below is 0, so without this the infimum would be junk.

The dispatch names three geometric inputs (h̄ from thm:yamabe (b), the boundary Yamabe inequality on D_j, the mean-curvature flip). The chain carries three more, and each is named. (1) The conformal law eq:conformal-energy-bdry for u on Σ (cited, l.326–328), because CurvedMetric carries R and H as free data: EH(Σ, h), computed from h's curvatures, meets the conformal quotient of u over g (where lem:kobayashi (a) lives) only through the law. (2) BoundaryMatch: B_j carries one area measure, seen from Σ or from D_j (A_j := Vol(B_j, h̄), l.663). (3) tr u = val u on B_j. The conformal identities of l.680 are proved, not carried.

R_g x = c for every x (pointwise, since m = min(0, min_Σ R_g) is a pointwise infimum).
MinimalBoundary g.

hypotheses.paper: lem:gluing: g̃_τ → g and R_{g̃_τ} → R_g uniformly, H_{g̃_τ} ≡ 0, ḡ_τ on Σ̄ with ḡ_τ|_Σ = g̃_τ and ḡ_τ|_{D_j} conformally flat (l.724)
hypotheses.note: the family gs : ι → CurvedMetric X N over a filter l ≠ ⊥, with UniformlyClose (η τ) g g̃_τ, η → 0 (the strict reading of 'uniformly', OQ-44), and |R_{g̃_τ} − R_g| ≤ δ τ, δ → 0. Per τ: minimal boundary, finite volume, Σ and B_j nonempty, measurable densities, and a GluingInput holding the gluing estimate's inputs with β = c_N.

hypotheses.paper: lem:gluing-estimate applied to (Σ̄, ḡ_τ), after dropping its non-positive last term (l.724–726)
hypotheses.note: proved: Filling.le_neg_infF_of_gluing and GluingInput.le_neg_infF, from gluing_estimate and inf F ≤ F(u) (u admissible, F ≥ 0).

hypotheses.paper: m_τ Vol(Σ, g̃_τ)^{2/N} → R_g Vol(Σ, g)^{2/N} and inf F_{g̃_τ} → inf F_g (l.728)
hypotheses.note: proved: CurvedMetric.tendsto_kobM, MeasuredModel.tendsto_vol_of_uniformlyClose, the strict tendsto_infF_of_uniformlyClose (lem:stability), giving kobM_mul_le_neg_infF.

hypotheses.paper: Y_[g](Σ) = EH(Σ, g) = R_g Vol(Σ, g)^{2/N} (l.724, lem:kobayashi (a))
hypotheses.note: the strict Y_eq_const_mul, which needs every val u a.e.-strongly measurable (hD).
MeasuredModel.infF over Adm (0 < ‖u‖²_{p*} < ∞), OQ-44.

findings: Minor, a citation in the proof (l.724; prop:nonpositive l.477–480; thm:upper-bound l.495). 'By Proposition prop:nonpositive, or directly by hypothesis, R_g ≤ 0 is constant.' prop:nonpositive assumes Σ̄ enlargeable. thm:upper-bound assumes only σ(Σ̄) ≤ 0, which enlargeability implies but which does not imply it (argued, not formalized: the K3 surface, N = 4, has σ = 0 and is simply connected, hence not enlargeable). None of thm:upper-bound's hypotheses states R_g ≤ 0. Without R_g ≤ 0, the limit of l.728 is min(0, R_g) Vol(Σ, g)^{2/N}, not R_g Vol(Σ, g)^{2/N}, and Y_[g](Σ) = R_g Vol^{2/N} (lem:kobayashi (a)) needs R_g ≤ 0. The gap closes inside the proof. The limit gives min(0, R_g) Vol(Σ, g)^{2/N} ≤ −inf F_g (Lean Yamabe.MeasuredModel.kobM_mul_le_neg_infF). lem:positivity gives inf F_g > 0, and the proof already uses it for cor:negative at l.728. Together they force R_g < 0, hence Y_[g](Σ) = R_g Vol^{2/N} ≤ −inf F_g (Yamabe.MeasuredModel.upper_bound_of_limit_of_pos, upper_bound_of_gluings_of_pos). Suggested fix: replace the appeal to prop:nonpositive at l.724 by this argument, or add 'Σ̄ enlargeable' to thm:upper-bound. The theorem's statement is not affected.
questions: 'R_g → uniformly' (l.724, l.728) is read as sup_x |R_{g̃_τ}(x) − R_g(x)| ≤ δ_τ → 0, and 'g̃_τ → g uniformly' as the strict UniformlyClose of lem:stability (OQ-44). 'For τ > 0' is read as a family over any filter l ≠ ⊥ (τ → 0⁺ is one), with the per-τ inequality needed only eventually in the limit lemmas, and for every τ in the assemblies.

'Constant scalar curvature' is read pointwise (R_g x = c for every x), because m = min(0, min_Σ R_g) is a pointwise infimum (CurvedMetric.kobM). With R_g = c only a.e., the limit would give kobM·Vol^{2/N}, which may be smaller than c·Vol^{2/N}.

This target formalizes the paper's own steps (l.724–728) and the assembly upper_bound_of_gluings. The inputs remain cited and carried: lem:gluing (the family g̃_τ, AB Thm 4.6 and a Seeley extension), thm:yamabe (b) on (Σ̄, ḡ_τ), fact (iv) (β_j = c_N), the conformal law, the flip, and prop:nonpositive or lem:positivity. Which of them become named externals is T-yamabe-scope's ruling.

kb_proposals: Conformal metrics on the frame model: with h.G = u^{4/(N−2)} • g.G and u > 0, vol_h = u^{p*} vol_g and bvol_h = u^{p♯} bvol_g are provable (Yamabe.sqrt_det_smul from Matrix.det_smul). FrameMetric carries no measurability, so the identity needs the density √det G to be AEMeasurable (MeasuredModel.DensityMeasurable). lintegral_withDensity_eq_lintegral_mul_non_measurable₀ needs only that, and takes any integrand (YamabeScaffold.Gluing: vol_conformal_univ, normSq_pStar_conformal, normSq_pSharp_conformal).

The filling of Σ by the D_j: Yamabe.Filling (one MeasuredModel Y E N 1 per piece, plus a measurable gluing map X → Y) and Yamabe.GluedMetric (body, cap j). The inputs are Props named after their lines (IsYamabeMetric, ConformalLaw, ConformalLawB, MeanCurvatureFlip, BoundaryMatch, BoundaryYamabe), bundled in Yamabe.GluingInput for assemblies over a family of metrics (T-yamabe-gluing-algebra).
A literal -1 passed through unification to an implicit {m : ℝ} can elaborate as Real.neg 1, which norm_num does not close. Give (m := -1) explicitly (toy_gluing_estimate).

Real.iInf over an empty type is 0 (Real.iInf_of_isEmpty), so CurvedMetric.kobM = 0 on an empty model and the volume is 0. Case on isEmpty_or_nonempty X before using ciInf_const or le_ciInf (tendsto_kobM, upper_bound_of_limit).
